cheats.title: Set up the Bioconda channels (once)
cheats.cmd:
conda config --add channels bioconda
conda config --add channels conda-forge
conda config --set channel_priority strict
cheats.notes: The order Bioconda recommends: conda-forge ends up first, then bioconda

cheats.title: environment.yml template
cheats.cmd:
name: {{env:rnaseq}}
channels:
  - conda-forge
  - bioconda
dependencies:
  - python=3.11
  - fastqc
  - multiqc
  - samtools
  - salmon

cheats.title: Conda version, config and paths
Faster installs with mamba
cheats.notes: mamba takes the same commands as conda. Miniforge includes it; conda 23.10+ already uses the faster libmamba solver by default

cheats.title: Install mamba
Intel-only Bioconda tool on an Apple Silicon Mac
cheats.cmd:
CONDA_SUBDIR=osx-64 conda create -n {{env}} -c conda-forge -c bioconda {{packages}} -y
conda activate {{env}} && conda config --env --set subdir osx-64
cheats.notes: Many Bioconda tools have no arm64 build yet; this makes an x86 env that runs under Rosetta. The second line keeps future installs in that env x86 too

cheats.title: Keep envs out of a small home quota (HPC)
cheats.notes: Or make it the default for every env:  conda config --add envs_dirs /scratch/$USER/envs

cheats.title: Move the package cache somewhere bigger (HPC)
Use a conda env inside a Slurm job script
cheats.notes: conda activate on its own often fails in batch jobs because conda init never ran in that shell

cheats.title: Make an env show up as a Jupyter kernel
cheats.cmd:
conda install -n {{env}} -c conda-forge ipykernel -y
conda run -n {{env}} python -m ipykernel install --user --name {{env}}
